record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: For a regular bounded potential V(x,t) that is localized in space and positive but may depend on time, can the time-dependent Schrödinger equation i∂tψ = -∆ψ + V(x,t)ψ have localized solutions? In the broader formulation, if the frozen operator -∆ + V(x,t) has no bound states for every fixed time t, must the full time-dependent equation have no localized solutions in any spatial dimension?

evidence.quote: 14.2. Quantum Ping-Pong. This is another fundamental question with a straightforward formulation: Can a positive potential, which is localized in space, bounded, and a regular function, have bound states? Such a potential must be time-dependent.

The broader question is: assuming the operator − ∆ + V (x,t ) has no bound states for each fixed t, does it follow that the equation i∂ψ ∂t = − ∆ψ +V (x,t )ψ has NO localized solutions? This remains an open problem in any dimension.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a bounded, smooth, nonnegative function that is spatially localized (e.g., $V(x,t)\to 0$ as $|x|\to\infty$ uniformly in $t$, and compactly supported in $x$ for each $t$). Consider the time-dependent Schrödinger equation
$$ i\,\partial_t\psi(x,t) = -\Delta\psi(x,t) + V(x,t)\psi(x,t),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ t\in\mathbb{R}. $$
A solution $\psi\in C(\mathbb{R};L^2(\mathbb{R}^n))$ is called localized if it remains spatially localized for all time, e.g., $\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}\int_{|x|>R}|\psi(x,t)|^2\,dx \to 0$ as $R\to\infty$.

(a) Can such a $V$ (with the properties above) admit a nontrivial localized solution $\psi$?

(b) (Broader formulation.) Assume in addition that for every fixed $t\in\mathbb{R}$ the self-adjoint operator $-\Delta + V(\cdot,t)$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ has no bound states (i.e., purely absolutely continuous spectrum). Does it follow that the time-dependent equation above has no nontrivial localized solution? Resolve this in every spatial dimension $n\ge 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The "quantum ping-pong" question—whether a smooth, bounded, positive, spatially localized time-dependent potential can support a localized solution of the Schrödinger equation, and the stronger version assuming the frozen operator has no bound states—is described in current literature as an open problem in all spatial dimensions. Web search did not turn up a published resolution.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as open in any dimension.
